text:
Ensembling machine learning models improves performance, but deploying an ensemble of large neural nets is often too computationally expensive [P3_p1_c02]. This paper solves the problem of deploying cumbersome models—such as ensembles or models trained with dropout—by transferring their knowledge into a single, smaller model suitable for deployment, using a process called distillation [P3_p1_c03]. 

While training requires extracting structure from large datasets without real-time constraints, deployment demands low latency and computational resources [P3_p1_c03]. A conceptual block in knowledge transfer is identifying knowledge exclusively with learned parameter values [P3_p1_c04]. Instead, the paper views knowledge more abstractly, freeing it from a particular instantiation [P3_p1_c04]. 

For tasks like MNIST, much information resides in the ratios of very small probabilities in the soft targets, which define a rich similarity structure over the data [P3_p2_c04]. Caruana and collaborators addressed this by using the logits as targets and minimizing the squared difference between the cumbersome and small models [P3_p2_c04]. Distillation generalizes this by raising the temperature of the final softmax until the cumbersome model produces a soft set of targets, and using that same high temperature when training the small model [P3_p2_c04]. 

Additionally, the paper introduces ensembles composed of full models and specialist models designed to learn fine-grained classes that the full models confuse [P3_p1_c02]. Specialists are assigned to classes by applying an on-line version of the K-means clustering algorithm to the columns of the covariance matrix of the generalist model's predictions [P3_p6_c03]. 

In experiments, training 10 separate models with different random initializations created sufficient diversity for the ensemble to outperform individual models [P3_p5_c02]. For distillation, temperatures of [1, 2, 5, 10] were tried and a relative weight of 0.5 was used on the cross-entropy for the hard targets [P3_p5_c02]. More than 80% of the improvement in frame classification accuracy from the 10-model ensemble was successfully transferred to the distilled model [P3_p5_c02].
